title: Time series database
summary: A time series database (TSDB) is software optimized for chronological data sequences, distinct from relational databases that model discrete relationships. TSDBs handle high ingestion rates through specialized compression like delta encoding or Gorilla compression, and automate data lifecycle management via bulk downsampling or deletion. They are purpose-built for append-only workloads from IoT, monitoring, and finance, organizing data with key-value tags for temporal and metadata queries. While supporting analytical tasks such as anomaly detection and forecasting, these capabilities are typically implemented via embedded machine-learning functions rather than native engine architecture.

mechanisms.title: Specialized compression algorithms
mechanisms.explanation: TSDBs achieve higher data density than standard techniques by utilizing compression methods tailored to the sequential uniformity of temporal data, such as delta encoding or Gorilla compression.

mechanisms.title: Automated data lifecycle management
mechanisms.explanation: TSDBs natively automate storage reduction by downsampling or dropping entire historical data partitions in bulk, reducing footprints and accelerating queries compared to general-purpose databases.
